title: Google Photos adds a new AI ‘Video Remix’ tool
author: [[Aisha Malik]]
description: The feature can do things like apply cinematic relighting to brighten up a dark clip, swap out a plain background for something fun, or add artistic styles to videos.

title: Meta just launched a new AI generator, Muse Image, and users are already pushing back over use of their photos
author: [[Lucas Ropek]]
description: The new image-generating model has numerous use cases, including advertising and decorating, and creator-based opportunities.

title: This startup pits dealerships against each other to bid on your used car
author: [[Sean O'Kane]]
description: Bidbus, which lets dealerships bid on used cars, has raised $15 million in a Series A round that was led by early-stage mobility fund Ibex Investors.

title: OpenAI is shutting down Atlas, but its AI browser ambitions are still growing
author: [[Rebecca Bellan]]
description: OpenAI is sunsetting its AI-powered browser after less than a year. But it's moving some agentic browsing features to its desktop app and a Chrome extension.

title: Discord admits AI moderation bug wrongfully banned users over harmless images
author: [[Lauren Forristal]]
description: The company confirmed that the issue had been affecting accounts since May, with an additional 200 users banned over the weekend before its team identified and fixed the problem.

title: Charles Hudson shares the common mistakes he’s seen after investing in 500+ startups
author: [[Maggie Nye]]
description: In this week’s episode of Build Mode, Isabelle Johannessen talks with Precursor Ventures' Charles Hudson about the headwinds facing early-stage founders today and the most common mistakes founders should avoid in order to get funded.

title: Paris-based AI voice startup Gradium raises $100M seed, backed by Nvidia
author: [[Julie Bort]]
description: The company is using the cash to open an office in the Bay Area and compete for talent there, "strengthening its position at the heart of the world's leading AI ecosystem."

title: Final extension: Startup Battlefield Australia applications now close July 20
author: [[Isabelle Johannessen]]
description: If you're building something ambitious, this is a fast track to the people who can move your startup forward.

title: US investors will soon get access to SK Hynix, another memory maker riding the AI boom
author: [[Julie Bort]]
description: SK Hynix is experiencing a boom credited to AI. It will ride that to a multibillion-dollar U.S. IPO, expected to take place on Friday.

title: SK Hynix raises $26.5B in the biggest foreign IPO in US history, is urged to build new US fabs
author: [[Kate Park]]
description: The AI chip boom just produced its biggest Wall Street moment yet. Now SK Hynix and Samsung are being asked to build U.S. factories.

title: Crypto VC firm Paradigm raises $1.2B to invest in ‘technical frontier’ startups
author: [[Dominic-Madori Davis]]
description: For Paradigm, the technical frontier will stretch beyond its cryptocurrency investment roots. This fund is expected to expand its investment focus to include robotics and AI.

title: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch on the fight to split off models from agents
author: [[Russell Brandom]]
description: "The reality is, when you're optimizing for production, you start looking at a price/performance," Guillermo Rauch tells TechCrunch.

title: OpenAI launches its new family of models with GPT-5.6
author: [[Lucas Ropek]]
description: OpenAI's latest family of models promises improvements across a range of areas, including cybersecurity.

title: Microsoft lays off nearly 5,000 employees across Xbox, commercial sales
author: [[Rebecca Bellan]]
description: Microsoft cut around 4,800 roles, or 2.1% of its global workforce, on Monday — the latest in a series of layoffs that’s stoking fears of AI replacing jobs. The layoffs will hit Xbox and commercial sales the hardest.

title: How did the government decide OpenAI’s frontier model was safe to release?
author: [[Tim Fernholz]]
description: "Exactly what that dialog looked like between the government and Anthropic and OpenAI is unclear."

title: Google will now disclose which ads are made with AI
author: [[Sarah Perez]]
description: While Google prohibits misleading and deceptive ads, an ad can still leverage AI to create some type of synthetic or digitally altered content. Until now, that's something Google only required election ads to disclose.

title: These AI startups are growing revenue at faster and faster rates
author: [[Marina Temkin]]
description: There are a lot of fast-growing AI startups, but some are growing even faster, they say.

title: Smart glasses maker Even Realities hits $1B valuation with $150M funding led by Meituan, Tencent
author: [[Kate Park]]
description: Even Realities, an ex-Apple team building camera-free smart glasses, raised $150M from Meituan and Tencent at a $1B valuation.

title: OpenAI says GPT 5.6 is the ‘preferred model’ for Microsoft Copilot 365 amid breakup chatter
author: [[Lucas Ropek]]
description: OpenAI's new family of models will continue to power Microsoft's suite of workplace and productivity apps.

title: If you use Google, you’re training its AI. Here’s how to opt out.
author: [[Sarah Perez]]
description: Consider this a belated PSA: A recent change to Google’s privacy settings is allowing the company to store more of your data, including media such as “images, files, and audio and video recordings,” to improve its AI models.

title: Microsoft joins AI cost-cutting trend by relying more on its own models
author: [[Lucas Ropek]]
description: Microsoft is the latest Silicon Valley giant to cut back on its AI spending.

title: Meta’s new AI chips will begin production in September
author: [[Ram Iyer]]
description: The company is taking a modular approach to designing these chips, anticipating that their needs will change as AI evolves rapidly by the time the chips are in production.

title: Meta removes controversial AI feature on Instagram after backlash
author: [[Lucas Ropek]]
description: "Our intent was to provide a useful creative tool and to give people control over whether their public content could be referenced in this way," the company said in a blog post. "We've heard the feedback that this feature missed the mark, so it's no longer available."

title: Reed Jobs would rather talk about curing cancer than his last name
author: [[Connie Loizos]]
description: When we last sat down with Jobs at TechCrunch Disrupt nearly three years ago, his firm Yosemite was brand new and biotech was still reeling from its post-pandemic crash. Now, the venture outfit has a team of 17; a cluster of blockbuster drugs are all losing patent protection in roughly the same window, creating all kinds of new opportunities; and AI has gone from a curiosity to, in Jobs's words, a huge part of what Yosemite does. "I didn't expect Yosemite to be moving this fast," he said.

title: Instagram users: Here’s how to stop Meta’s AI from using your photos
author: [[Lauren Forristal]]
description: Muse Image allows users to generate AI images using photos from public Instagram accounts. As long as a person's profile is public, another user can tag that account and use their images as part of an AI-generated creation.

title: Why this CEO thinks video games make better training data than the internet
author: [[Theresa Loconsolo]]
description: When it comes to achieving artificial general intelligence (AGI), large language models just don’t have what it takes. Models like ChatGPT and Claude are great at text, but they’re less skilled at understanding how things actually move through space and time — an essential skill for producing intelligence that generalizes. That gap, it turns out, might be filled by gaming data. That’s the bet behind General Intuition, a […]

title: Elon Musk praises Mythos/Fable, promises not to ‘cut off’ Anthropic
author: [[Julie Bort]]
description: Should Anthropic trust Elon Musk to host its models? With about $40 billion in revenue at stake, Musk insists that the company can.

title: This startup thinks robotics is about to have its ChatGPT moment
author: [[Rebecca Bellan]]
description: General Intuition is betting millions of hours of video game data can train the foundation models for physical AI, making it easier to build smarter robots with minimal real-world data.

title: Meta wants its AI glasses to seem less creepy. Its AI strategy says otherwise.
author: [[Sarah Perez]]
description: Meta is adding a new safeguard to stop people from secretly recording others with its AI glasses. But the update comes as the company continues to expand how much personal data its AI products collect and use.

title: An AI agent startup just let its agent run its $100M fundraise
author: [[Connie Loizos]]
description: Lyzr, a startup that builds AI agents for enterprises, used its own AI agent to raise a $100 million round — proof, evidently, that the product actually works.

title: Filing: College app Fizz accuses VC of sharing confidential startup information with rival Sidechat
author: [[Sarah Perez]]
description: Fizz has expanded its lawsuit against rival Sidechat, alleging that a Maveron VC shared its confidential information obtained during a fundraising meeting with the competing startup.

title: Savi’s app aims to protect consumers from realistic AI scams like kidnappers demanding ransom
author: [[Julie Bort]]
description: The company just raised $7 million in seed funding, and is launching its app for iPhone and Android on Tuesday.

title: With EU backing, QuantumDiamonds aims to speed up chip manufacturing
author: [[Anna Heim]]
description: Like its U.S. counterpart, the European Chips Act aims to foster the semiconductor industry — in part thanks to state subsidies. One of the beneficiaries is QuantumDiamonds, a German startup that applies a novel approach to inspecting chips.

title: You can now customize Siri’s pace and expressivity in the latest iOS 27 beta
author: [[Sarah Perez]]
description: The update is part of Apple's broader effort to make Siri feel more natural and personal, as it rebuilds the assistant around generative AI.

title: OpenAI releases new voice models for more natural live conversations
author: [[Ivan Mehta]]
description: OpenAI says its new voice mode can speak and listen at the same time, a key ability for live translation.

title: Meta enters the crowded AI coding battle with Muse Spark 1.1
author: [[Lucas Ropek]]
description: Meta's pitch to users is Spark's ability to handle large agentic workloads, fix bugs, and help with large code migrations — the kind of automation that enterprises are increasingly turning to AI companies to provide.

title: Autonomous drone delivery startup Manna plots major US expansion
author: [[Kirsten Korosec]]
description: Manna is launching a U.S. operations and manufacturing facility in Tulsa, Oklahoma, that will eventually employ 1,000 people.

title: Station F ramps up as a launchpad for Europe’s hottest AI startups
author: [[Anna Heim]]
description: Station F, a Paris-based startup hub founded by French billionaire Xavier Niel, is gearing up for a new edition of its F/ai accelerator program in a bid to strengthen its positioning as a stepping stone for promising AI startups.

title: Hugging Face’s CEO on why companies are done renting their AI
author: [[Theresa Loconsolo]]
description: Open source AI is booming, according to Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue. The company has grown into something like a GitHub for AI in recent years, where AI builders can share and download open models and datasets, now used by roughly half the Fortune 500. Delangue has seen the same story play out again and again: companies start […]

title: AI law startup Norm raises $120M, hits unicorn valuation
author: [[Dominic-Madori Davis]]
description: AI law startup Norm has raised a $120 million Series C round led by Khosla Ventures, valuing the startup at $1.2 billion.

title: Phia accused of ‘cookie stuffing,’ taking affiliate credit on purchases it didn’t earn
author: [[Dominic-Madori Davis]]
description: Phia, the shopping startup founded by Bill Gates’ daughter, Phoebe, and her friend Sophia Kianni is under fire for a practice known as “cookie stuffing,” which helped the product receive commissions and credit for sales it did not actually generate, per a Bloomberg investigation.

title: Every major tech layoff in 2026 that has name-checked AI
author: [[Rebecca Bellan, Connie Loizos]]
description: A running look — in reverse chronological order — at the bigger tech companies that have announced significant layoffs this year with AI as a stated factor.

title: Prime Intellect raises $130M Series A to help enterprises build their own AI agents
author: [[Marina Temkin]]
description: Founded in 2024, Prime Intellect’s goal is to give organizations capabilities to train their own agentic systems without relying on frontier AI labs.

title: Almost 90 new unicorns have been minted so far this year — here they are
author: [[Dominic-Madori Davis]]
description: With AI igniting an investor frenzy, more startups are achieving unicorn status every month.

title: Solo GP Ashley Smith announces second $25M fund to back startups in AI, security and more
author: [[Dominic-Madori Davis]]
description: Vermilion Cliffs Ventures announced Wednesday the close of a $25 million Fund II.

title: Hot French startup ZML releases free product to speed inference across lots of AI chips
author: [[Anna Heim]]
description: ZML, a hot French AI startup endorsed by Turing Award winner Yann LeCun, has now released ZML/LLMD, software that could make running AI less costly.

title: The ‘first’ AI-run ransomware attack still needed a human
author: [[Connie Loizos]]
description: An AI agent carried out the technical execution of a real-world ransomware attack for the first known time, but new details show a human still chose the victim, set up the infrastructure, and supplied stolen credentials — meaning it wasn't quite the fully autonomous cybercrime debut that last week's headlines suggested.

title: Fidji Simo steps down from OpenAI’s no. 2 role
author: [[Connie Loizos]]
description: OpenAI's No. 2 executive, Fidji Simo, is stepping down from her full-time role after her medical leave proved longer than expected — a leadership vacuum that comes at a tricky time as the company eyes a possible IPO and races to catch Anthropic in the enterprise market.

title: Reddit is using LLMs to solve a problem LLMs largely created
author: [[Amanda Silberling]]
description: In the AI era, platforms have no choice but to fight fire with fire to cull spam.

title: Why the rise of open source AI isn’t hurting Anthropic … yet
author: [[Russell Brandom]]
description: Open source models’ success isn’t coming at the expense of frontier labs. Instead, they each seem to capture two phases of the same life cycle.

title: AI chip maker SambaNova raises $1B at $11B valuation, 5 months after last mega round
author: [[Kate Park]]
description: AI chip maker SambaNova has raised at an $11B valuation months after Intel was rumored to be trying to buy it for about $1.6 billion.

title: Can AI answer the $3 trillion question?
author: [[Tim Fernholz]]
description: The AI ROI debate has returned and the numbers are even bigger, as are, perhaps, the consequences.

title: SpaceXAI releases Grok 4.5, which Elon describes as an ‘Opus-class model’
author: [[Lucas Ropek]]
description: Elon Musk's tech company released the newest version of Grok on Wednesday, promising a cheaper, more efficient alternative to other powerful AI models.

title: Figma acquires team behind a vibe-coding app
author: [[Ivan Mehta]]
description: The Y Combinator-backed company started a vibe-coding platform and later built an agent-creation product.

title: This humanoid robotics company is going public, but its CEO isn’t promising a robot in your home anytime soon
author: [[Connie Loizos]]
description: While other humanoid startups chase sky-high valuations, Agility Robotics is betting its future on execution — and a SPAC.

title: Google’s deepfake detector system used to debunk McConnell hoax pic
author: [[Russell Brandom]]
description: Earlier this week, a picture seemed to show Kentucky Senator Mitch McConnell covered in tubes in a hospital bed in a state of extreme distress. It turned out to be an AI-generated fake.
